prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2010 – Change that works for you: building a fairer, greener, more democratic Britain.

Core belief: Britain’s problems stem from power being hoarded by Westminster and big business. The answer is fairness—distributing economic, social and political power so everyone has opportunity and voice.

Four priorities
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
  - No income tax on the first £10,000, a £700 tax cut for most, lifting 3.6m low earners and pensioners out of tax.
  - Paid for by fairness at the top: equal CGT and income tax rates; basic-rate pension tax relief for all; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; per‑plane duty on aviation (with higher rates for unnecessary domestic flights); a crackdown on avoidance/evasion; time‑limited non‑dom status (max 7 years).
  - Honest deficit plan: over £15bn identified savings; a Council on Financial Stability; protect frontline services by cutting waste (ID cards, quangos, Eurofighter Tranche 3B), reforming public pay/pensions, and not replacing Trident like‑for‑like.

- A fair chance for every child
  - £2.5bn Pupil Premium targeted at disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one support; early SEN assessment; tougher anti‑bullying (including homophobic bullying); better teacher training.
  - Free schools to innovate via an Education Freedom Act; local accountability, not Whitehall control; inclusive faith school admissions.
  - Replace rigid curriculum/testing with a minimum entitlement; merge academic and vocational routes via a General Diploma; 14–19s free to study at college.
  - Scrap tuition fees, phased over six years (immediate for final‑year students); targeted bursaries; expand apprenticeships and foundation degrees.

- A fair future: jobs and growth by making Britain greener
  - Break up the banks; responsible lending; curb bonus culture; banking levy; grow local finance (Local Enterprise Funds, Regional Stock Exchanges).
  - Green stimulus creating 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 eco cash‑back for home efficiency/micro‑generation; insulate public buildings with a rolling fund; bring 250,000 empty homes back into use; low‑carbon bus scrappage.
  - UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for clean energy, rail, and broadband.
  - Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050: 40% of electricity from clean sources by 2020 (prioritising marine/offshore); block unabated coal; reject new nuclear as poor value; a 10‑year home insulation drive; European Supergrid; stronger ETS and EU 30% cut by 2020.
  - Transport fairness: cut regulated rail fares in real terms; empower councils on buses; cancel Heathrow’s third runway; replace APD with per‑plane duty; zero‑emission new cars by 2040.

- A fair deal by cleaning up politics and defending liberties
  - Give people power: STV for fair votes (fewer MPs), fixed terms, a fully elected second chamber, recall for corrupt MPs, cap donations at £10k, robust lobbying transparency, and UK‑tax‑paying representatives.
  - Restore civil liberties with a Freedom Bill: scrap ID cards and mass data retention; end control orders; cut pre‑charge detention to 14 days; allow intercept evidence; remove innocent DNA; protect the Human Rights Act; defend free speech and libel reform.
  - Devolve power and finance to nations and communities; fair local taxation; elected police authorities and health boards.

A safer, fairer society and world
- 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; focus on what works (youth services, rehabilitation, restorative justice; presumption against short sentences).
- Firm and fair immigration: exit checks; a National Border Force; regional points‑based work routes; earned citizenship for long‑settled, law‑abiding people; end child detention; dignified, independent asylum system.
- NHS protected by cutting waste; integrate health and social care; priority for cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia; clean air and alcohol harm reduction.
- Dignity for families and older people: shared parental leave, flexible work for all, carers’ respite, scrap compulsory retirement age, restore the pensions earnings link.
- International leadership rooted in values: full defence review; no like‑for‑like Trident; pro‑EU cooperation; lawful counter‑terrorism; critical support in Afghanistan; push for global disarmament, fair finance, development (0.7% aid), and climate justice.

If you want real, lasting change grounded in fairness—choose the Liberal Democrats.
